current_donor.relationship: The current donor names an older external wache-koenig.py as the blocking predecessor, but the pinned donor does not contain that installed-host artifact. This delta recovers the exact historical precursor bytes from the archived Drive identity only.

atoms.what_it_does: Parses hook JSON and gates only tool_name == Bash. Malformed hook JSON exits 0, non-Bash tools exit 0, /tmp/claude-* scratch deletions matching KRITZEL exit 0. Hard-deny or missing-ticket decisions exit 2 before Bash execution when this script is actually installed as a blocking PreToolUse guard.
atoms.why: Useful historical blocking semantics exist, but the guard is Bash-scoped and includes deliberate fail-open/bypass classes. It is not a complete EntityOS effect authority.

atoms.what_it_does: Classifies unconditional hard-deny operations (format/raw-device writes), ticket-required destructive operations, destructive DB statements, and destructive commands nested inside ssh/bash-c style command strings. Heredoc bodies and ordinary quoted arguments are stripped before ordinary command-position matching to reduce false positives.
atoms.why: Command-position parsing and nested-command reinspection are reusable historical ideas, but regex command parsing must remain a narrow adapter rather than canonical capability semantics.

atoms.what_it_does: Looks up a ticket by the first 16 hex chars of sha256(command), verifies the full stored command hash and validity window, deletes expired tickets, and deletes a valid ticket before returning allow. The permit is therefore command-bound and one-shot at source level.
atoms.why: Exact-operation binding plus consume-before-execution is a strong predecessor invariant. Frankenstein 2.0 should generalize it to immutable invocation identity, generation, capability and policy provenance rather than command text alone.

atoms.what_it_does: Requires /dev/tty, requests two sequential fresh random transcription challenges, rejects too-fast challenge entry and nearly identical challenge timings, then writes a chmod-0600 command-hash-bound ticket with valid_from = issue+600s and valid_until = issue+1800s.
atoms.why: The /dev/tty separation is a useful historical human-presence barrier. Typing-time heuristics are convenience/anti-self-approval measures, not identity authority, and should not become a canonical authorization primitive.

atoms.what_it_does: For local rm, attempts to measure named targets with du -sb, refuses unmeasurable wildcard/shell targets, and rejects requests above 300 MB per approval. Remote ssh deletion is not subject to this local size calculation.
atoms.why: Bounded blast-radius policy is reusable, but must be expressed as typed effect budget/capability policy rather than filename heuristics.

atoms.what_it_does: The source explicitly states that /tmp/claude-* scratch remains ungated and that the guard can be modified by its own user unless file ownership/mode is externally hardened (suggested root:root 0644).
atoms.why: A guard writable by the same execution principal and scoped away from some mutation classes cannot by itself establish tamper-resistant canonical effect authority.

architecture_consequences.rule: Do not collapse HISTORICAL_SOURCE_EXACT_BYTES into CURRENT_HOST_ENFORCEMENT. Current enforcement credit requires exact installed settings/hook order/artifact digest plus an observed blocking receipt at invocation identity.
useful_donor_primitives: human-channel separation from the AI tool invocation
must_not_promote: Bash-only coverage to whole effect coverage
regex classifier to canonical capability semantics
typing heuristics to authenticated human identity
historical Drive source to current installed-host source
source exit-2 path to runtime-observed blocking without loaded-hook evidence
architecture_consequences.frankenstein_2_successor_contract: HumanIntentDecision -> Task/CapabilityAdmission -> invocation-bound pre-side-effect EnforcementDecision -> one-shot EnforcementReceipt -> ExecutionReceipt -> effect-class-specific WorldEffectVerification -> ResultReentry -> typed CompletionEvidence. Historical command-hash tickets may inform the one-shot binding but cannot replace tool_use_id/invocation_id, generation or policy provenance.

counterhypotheses.claim: The currently installed host-global guard may still be byte-identical to recovered wache-koenig.py and therefore provide real Bash blocking today.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Resolve loaded Claude settings/hook order and hash the actually invoked host artifact; then run only an authorized harmless deny/non-execution probe in Triggerword-4/runtime lane.

counterhypotheses.claim: Bash may be the only mutating child capability on the installed runtime, making Bash-only coverage sufficient for that specific actor class.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Enumerate installed mutating tool/capability classes for HEADLESS_SESSION_CHILD and NATIVE_SUBAGENT_CHILD separately; any non-Bash mutation path falsifies whole-child coverage.

contradictions_preserved: The historical external guard contains real source-level blocking semantics, while the current donor-internal EffectGate explicitly does not block ordinary tools. These are different mechanisms and must not be conflated.
Exact historical bytes are now recovered, but current host installation, settings composition and hook ordering remain unresolved.
The historical guard deliberately fails open for malformed input/non-Bash/scratch cases while current EntityOS effect authority aims for typed fail-closed state-changing boundaries.
